resources.string: Hold the sensor against the top back of the phone
Scan again at any time to refresh
Turn on NFC in the phone settings
A phone with NFC is needed to read the sensor
Not an ISO 15693 tag, so not a Libre sensor
Bluetooth address unknown. Turn on \"Enable BLE streaming\" and scan again.
1. Tap Share JSON and send it to the phone that has the Zepp app.\n2. In Zepp open AmazCGM settings → Paste JSON.\n3. On the watch open AmazCGM and tap Sync from phone.
Lets the watch pull the scan straight from this phone with Sync from phone. While visible, this phone is named AMZCGM in Bluetooth; its name is restored afterwards.
Allow "Nearby devices" so the watch can find this phone
Not fetched by the watch yet
On the watch open AmazCGM and tap Sync from phone
Read only: reports the sensor identity and, if a key was already generated, repeats it. Nothing is written to the sensor.
Writes the unlock code to the sensor and turns its Bluetooth on. This invalidates the key any other app or device is currently using for this sensor.
This is a generation-2 security sensor. Its BLE unlock is not covered by the open Libre 2 crypto, so the key cannot be derived here.
Sensor type %1$s does not use the Libre 2 BLE streaming protocol.
FRAM checksums did not validate, so the sensor data could not be confirmed. The keys may still be correct.
Typed unlock code %1$d was not written. The watch still gets %2$d from the last streaming enable. Turn on \"Enable BLE streaming\" and scan again to write %1$d.
